title: Angled launches
target: Use components to analyze an angled projectile.
criteria: Separate the initial velocity into two components.
Use vertical motion to determine flight time.
Explain the assumptions behind range comparisons.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A launch speed is 10 m/s at an angle with cosθ = 0.8 and sinθ = 0.6. What are initial horizontal and upward components?
cpa.guide: vx = v cosθ = 8; vy = v sinθ = 6.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A launch has horizontal component 9 m/s and upward component 12 m/s. What is launch speed?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Initial upward velocity is 8 m/s. Use g = 10 m/s² without drag. How long to the highest point?
cpa.guide: At top vy = 0; t = v_y0/g = 0.8 s.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A projectile launches with vx = 5 m/s and vy = 20 m/s upward, returning to launch height. Use g = 10 m/s² and no drag. What are total flight time and range?
cpa.guide: Time = 2vy/g = 4 s; range = vx t = 20 m.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Under which conditions does 45° maximize range for fixed launch speed?
options: Only when horizontal velocity is zero.
Equal launch/landing heights, uniform g, negligible air resistance.
All terrains and all drag forces.
cpa.guide: The familiar angle result depends on these ideal assumptions.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A projectile lands far below its launch height. Is 45° guaranteed to maximize range at fixed speed?
options: Yes; 45° is exact in every environment.
No; unequal heights change the flight-time and range relationship.
No; range must always be zero.
cpa.guide: The standard equal-height result cannot be applied uncritically.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
